_comment: Forum wallet-login v2, the bound approval, between warren-connect and every Warren client. A login completes only in the browser that opened it (the __Host-warren_login cookie set by /sso) AND with the one-time code returned to the wallet that signed the approval. v2 changes the approval request (an explicit login_version in the signed body), its answer (a completion object) and the browser half (the cookie, the confirm step, the handoff page). forum_login_v1.json keeps pinning the report and attach-logs wire, which v2 does not change, and the approval form that predates the code. Synthetic host, key, cookie and secret only. Adding a request or an answer name breaks the consumers until they handle it, on purpose.

signer._comment: The v1 signer: signing_key_hex is the raw 32-byte Ed25519 secret, timestamp the X-Warren-Timestamp value (outside any live provider's 60 s window, so these exact bytes replay onto clock_skew and their acceptance is proven with the provider clock at timestamp). connect_host stands in for the deployment's connect host.

requests.name: login_bound
requests._comment: A bound approval of the sign-in session named by the deep link, the QR or a typed sign-in code: the sid it carried plus login_version 2, compact, keys in ascending order. The same bytes whichever of the session's two ids the sid is; the provider tells them apart.

cookie._comment: Set by GET /sso on the approval page, reused when the browser already holds a well-formed one (a refresh and a second tab stay bound). HttpOnly: no script reads it, the page's own included. Only the provider's own pages send it; an app never holds it.
cookie.name: __Host-warren_login

handoff._comment: The URL a same-device approval returns in completion.handoff_url, for the approving app to open in its own default browser. The sid (the same-device id) and the code ride in the fragment only, which no browser sends to a server. The page posts the confirm with its cookie and completes, or tells a browser that did not open the login that it did not.

states._comment: Values of status in the browser's state document, and of reason when status is cancelled.

responses._comment: Status, Content-Type and exact body bytes per outcome, JSON keys in ascending order. The approved answers were produced under the provider parameters below with the provider's code draw fixed to provider.completion_code; a live provider draws the code at random, so a replay substitutes the code it received, and its own sid and connect host in handoff_url.

app_update_required._comment: An approval without login_version (the v1 form) refused: always for staff, and for everyone unless the deployment allows the legacy form. The browser's session is cancelled with reason app_update_required.

subscription_required.body_utf8: forum access requires a Warren subscription

session_unknown._comment: Unknown, expired, cancelled, or no longer waiting for an approval: a second approval never replaces the first.

session_status_app._endpoint: GET /v1/session/{sid}/status without the login cookie (the app's read before it signs; its Date header is the trusted clock). Either id.

session_status._endpoint: GET /v1/session/{sid}/status with the login cookie (the approval page's poll). Same-device id only.

browser_mismatch._comment: A cookie that is not the session's, or a sid naming no live session: the same answer.

confirm._endpoint: POST /v1/session/{sid}/confirm with the login cookie and Content-Type application/json. Same-device id only. Five wrong codes cancel the login.

not_awaiting_code._comment: The session's state document, here before the approval.

complete._endpoint: GET /v1/session/{sid}/complete with the login cookie, a top-level navigation. Same-device id only.

already_completed._comment: Another tab of the same browser completed first.

cancel._endpoint: POST /v1/session/{sid}/cancel, no cookie, no body: the app's decline. Either id; ends only a login still waiting for its approval, and answers the same for any id.

provider._comment: The synthetic deployment parameters the identity-bearing answers were produced under: handle and external_id are the keyed derivation over the signer key under handle_secret_utf8, notify_slot the slot drawn in that run, completion_code the code the provider's draw was fixed to, qr_sid the session's cross-device id, forum_public_url the forum origin (return_sso_url lives under it).
